headline: Google DeepMind reports AI-assisted machine-checked proofs for selected Signal protocol code properties
summary: Google DeepMind’s Nov 10 paper and public Lean repository report machine-checked symbolic and computational proofs for selected security properties of compiled AArch64 `libsignal` code in a CLI harness. The proofs concern the PQXDH handshake and Triple Ratchet and reportedly establish properties including forward secrecy, post-compromise security, authentication and confidentiality under the paper’s specifications. Human-guided specification and hooked primitive contracts are part of the proof boundary. The paper reports proof teams typically had 40–80 agents working on one machine for 24–72 hours; the public README says a clean full proof build takes several hours and peaks at about 15–34 GiB RAM. These figures describe proof campaigns and a verification build, not total project cost, human effort or demonstrated scalable economics. The work does not cover Signal’s mobile apps or server/group protocols, and the computational theorem has explicit cryptographic assumptions and attacker/model restrictions. WIRED notes prior Signal formal-verification work provided a head start. the research desk inspected the paper and repository page but did not build or independently replay the proofs.
